subject: chemistry
title: Addition polymerisation
key_idea: (Separate science) In addition polymerisation, many small alkene molecules called monomers join to make one very large molecule, a polymer. The C=C bond opens and no other molecule is made. So the repeating unit has the same atoms as the monomer.

blocks.text: (Separate science) Alkenes can be used to make polymers. Each alkene molecule has a C=C double bond, which opens so the molecules can join in a chain.

items.meaning: A small molecule that can join with many others to make a polymer.
A substance of high average relative molecular mass, made of small repeating units.
Many monomers join together with no other molecule formed.
The part of the polymer chain that repeats, written in brackets with n.

To find a monomer, put the C=C back into one repeating unit.

sections.heading: Properties and uses of addition polymers

blocks.text: (Separate science) The use of a polymer depends on its properties. A good answer links a property to the use, then gives the reason.

rows: Window frames, water pipes, insulation for electrical wires
Does not conduct electricity, waterproof, flexible, unreactive
Coating for frying pans, stain-proofing clothing

items: PVC insulates cables because it does not conduct electricity, so it separates the user from the current.
PTFE coats pans because it is non-stick, so food will not stick.
A food wrapping must be non-toxic, so it does not poison the food.
It could instead be unreactive, so it does not react with the food, or flexible, so it wraps all around the food.
Link each use to a property and give a reason.
PTFE is non-stick, PVC is an insulator, and poly(ethene) is flexible and unreactive.

checks.q: What type of molecule is the monomer in addition polymerisation, and what happens to its double bond?
checks.a: The monomer is an alkene (it contains C=C). The double bond opens so the monomers can join together in a chain.

checks.q: Draw or describe the repeating unit of poly(ethene).
checks.a: –CH₂–CH₂–, the repeating unit of poly(ethene) in brackets with n after it.

checks.q: State one use of PTFE and the property that makes it suitable.
checks.a: Coating frying pans, because it is non-stick (slippery), so food will not stick to the pan.

worked_example.tip: One mark for each word. The words must be in this order.

worked_example.question:
Poly(tetrafluoroethene) is also known as Teflon™.

State one use of poly(tetrafluoroethene) and explain how one of its properties makes it suitable for that use.
answer_points: Property: it is slippery or non-stick.
Reason: food will not stick to the (frying) pan.
worked_example.tip: One mark each for the use, the property and the reason. The property and reason must depend on the use.
